comparison: Both evaluations support the finding of reproducible island formation in albino mice (C1, C17, C18, C22, C120). OpenEval emphasizes reproducibility across 12/12 mice and consistency with prior work. Peer reviewers accept this as a 'naturally emerging case' that is 'clearly demonstrated' and 'consistent with previous literature.' Both also address activity-dependence (C2, C19), though OpenEval separates this into R2.

OpenEval R2 addresses activity-dependent island formation (C2, C19, C88-C90) as a separate supported finding based on prior work blocking retinal waves. Peer R1 includes C2 and C19 alongside island formation claims, accepting both without challenge. Both evaluations support these claims, though OpenEval notes reliance on prior work rather than new experiments.

Both evaluations strongly support the ultrastructural characterization of islands and exclusion zones (C20, C23-C36). OpenEval emphasizes that EM data rules out pathological interpretations and demonstrates organized synaptic structures. Peer reviewers accept these findings as 'morphological descriptions' with 'high resolution' achieved through serial EM, with no methodological concerns raised.

OpenEval R3 includes characterization of the exclusion zone (C25-C27, C33-C35) as part of broader ultrastructural findings. Peer R4 specifically addresses exclusion zone findings, accepting them as part of the 'complete synaptic isolation' mechanism. Both evaluations support these claims without challenge.

Both evaluations support the central finding of complete synaptic segregation (C3, C21, C44, C45, C50). OpenEval emphasizes the EM reconstruction of 15 TCs and Monte Carlo statistical validation (p<0.01), noting data from single animal. Peer reviewers describe evidence as 'compelling' with 'combined confocal imaging and serial EM reconstructions showing complete synaptic isolation,' clearly demonstrating segregation of misrouted axons.

OpenEval R4 includes statistical validation claims (C48, C49) as part of the segregation evidence. Peer R7 implicitly accepts the statistical analysis through acceptance of overall segregation findings, with no concerns raised about Monte Carlo approach. Both support the statistical methodology.

OpenEval R4 includes methodological claims about EM reconstruction (C40-C43) as part of segregation evidence. Peer R11 explicitly praises the methodological approach, noting 'Good use of CLEM' and 'high resolution' as major strengths. Both support the technical quality, though peer reviewers acknowledge limited sample size as inherent to demanding technique rather than criticism.

Both evaluations support dendritic asymmetry findings (C51, C52, C110). OpenEval emphasizes spatial segregation despite dendritic overlap potential, indicating organizational principles beyond synaptic selection. Peer reviewers accept these morphological observations as part of 'compelling' evidence, with prior concerns noted as resolved.

OpenEval R5 addresses dendritic asymmetry (C111, C112) as supported finding. Peer R10 includes these claims in discussion of dendritic pruning mechanism for exclusion zones, accepting the interpretation without objection. OpenEval treats asymmetry as established observation while peer evaluation encompasses it within mechanistic framework.

Both evaluations support the finding of cortical feedback synapses in exclusion zones (C53), demonstrating specificity of segregation to retinogeniculate connectivity. OpenEval emphasizes this rules out global segregation. Peer reviewers accept this finding as part of the overall demonstration without challenge.

Both evaluations support differential connectivity patterns in inhibitory circuitry (C54-C70, including C62-C65, C67, C70). OpenEval emphasizes cell-type-specific segregation extending to interneurons based on confocal and EM data. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'mixed connectivity onto LGN local interneurons' as key result and 'interesting difference between TC and LIN neurons' as strength.

Both evaluations support the main conclusion about complete segregation (C4, C71, C74). OpenEval emphasizes this demonstrates capacity for organization in albino case contrasting with normal intermixing. Peer R2 focuses on the central segregation finding with 'compelling' evidence. Both strongly affirm this core result.

OpenEval R8 includes claims about segregation capacity (C91, C92) as part of main conclusion. Peer R3 accepts these as part of ultrastructural findings demonstrating segregation. Both evaluations support these claims within their respective framings.

Both evaluations support the mechanistic interpretation involving Hebbian mechanisms (C83). OpenEval frames this as well-supported by combined anatomical and connectivity data. Peer reviewers explicitly frame study as examining 'role of Hebbian synapse rewiring' with 'compelling' evidence, emphasizing system's capacity to segregate inputs.

Both evaluations support the Hebbian mechanistic model (C93-C108, including C93, C107). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting model is consistent with established principles and cited literature, though remains theoretical framework not directly tested. Peer reviewers accept 'Hebbian predictions' as compelling framework. Both acknowledge this as reasonable inference rather than directly demonstrated mechanism.

Both evaluations address dendritic pruning hypothesis for exclusion zones (C109, C111, C112, C116). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting hypothesis is consistent with literature but lacks direct experimental support. Peer reviewers accept interpretation without objection, with satisfaction that concerns were addressed. This represents a key difference: OpenEval expresses uncertainty while peer reviewers accept the speculative mechanism.

Perfect claim overlap (C72, C73, C82). Both evaluations support the comparison to normal dLGN organization. OpenEval emphasizes citation to prior work (Morgan et al., 2016) establishing context. Peer reviewers explicitly discuss this context, noting 'retinal inputs typically do not segregate within the mouse dLGN' and accepting albino findings as demonstrating segregation capacity.

OpenEval R12 addresses comparative mammalian context (C75-C81, C84), supported by multiple citations. No corresponding peer evaluation found specifically addressing these comparative claims about mouse dLGN organization within broader mammalian evolution.

OpenEval R13 addresses molecular guidance mechanisms and glomerular formation (C85-C87), supported by citations. The inference about mistargeted axons is noted as hypothesis. No corresponding peer evaluation found specifically addressing these molecular mechanism claims.

OpenEval R14 addresses background on dLGN development (C5-C16), supported by extensive literature citations. No corresponding peer evaluation found specifically addressing these background/context claims, though peer reviewers implicitly accept this context.

OpenEval R15 addresses established principles of dLGN function (C37, C38), providing rationale for functional significance. No corresponding peer evaluation found specifically addressing these functional context claims.

OpenEval R16 rates claim C47 about superior colliculus inputs as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative interpretation not directly demonstrated. No corresponding peer evaluation found addressing this specific hypothesis about RGC convergence variability.

OpenEval R17 addresses methodological statements about animal subjects and ethics (C117-C119) as adequately documented. No corresponding peer evaluation found specifically addressing these standard reporting elements.
